input.title: SQL injection in public /orders/search via 'customer' query parameter
input.evidence: demo-store-api/app/main.py:15-18 - the route /orders/search reads `customer` straight from request.args. Nothing validates or authenticates it, and the docstring at line 17 says it backs the storefront's public order lookup page. main.py:20 puts `customer` into the SQL string with an f-string inside single quotes. main.py:21 runs it with conn.execute() against sqlite3 (app/db.py:8-11). Example payload: customer=' OR '1'='1 returns every order (ids, totals, statuses) for all customers. UNION-based payloads such as ' UNION SELECT name,sql,type FROM sqlite_master-- can read the schema and other tables. sqlite3's execute() runs only one statement, so stacked queries won't work, but reading any data is enough. Anyone can reach this without logging in.
input.recommended_fix: Use a parameterized query: conn.execute("SELECT id, total, status FROM orders WHERE customer_email = ?", (customer,)). Also think about whether a public endpoint should return orders by email alone without verifying the customer (IDOR / data exposure), and add rate limiting. Add a regression test that sends a quote payload.

input.title: False positive: /reports/status SQL value comes from a fixed allowlist
input.evidence: demo-store-api/app/main.py:28 reads the user-supplied `status` key. main.py:29 maps it through the REPORT_STATUSES dict (main.py:8-12) with .get(key, "OPEN"), so `status` can only be one of the constants "OPEN", "SHIPPED" or "REFUNDED". User input never reaches the f-string at main.py:31. Any key not in the dict becomes "OPEN". No injection is possible.
input.recommended_fix: No security fix is required. For defense in depth, and to silence the scanner, switch to a parameterized query: conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE status = ?", (status,)). Separately, check whether this operations-dashboard endpoint should require authentication (no auth is visible).

input.title: False positive: string-formatted INSERT in test seed data
input.evidence: demo-store-api/tests/test_search.py:13 builds an INSERT with an f-string, but the values come from the loop index and the hardcoded SEED_EMAILS constant (test_search.py:7, 12). The code runs only in the pytest seed() helper against a temporary DB (tmp_path, lines 18-20). It is not part of any HTTP route, so no attacker input reaches it.
input.recommended_fix: No security fix is needed. Optionally use placeholders (conn.execute("INSERT INTO orders VALUES (?, ?, 10.0, 'OPEN')", (i, email))) as good practice, or exclude tests/ from this rule.

content.text:
I read all three findings and the code behind them, and saved a draft ticket for each. They're waiting for human review. Only one finding is a real vulnerability: F-001 is an SQL injection on a public route that anyone can use without logging in. The other two are false positives.

| ID | Location | Verdict | Severity | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-001 | app/main.py:20 | **Exploitable** | **Critical** | The `customer` value from the request (main.py:18) goes straight into the SQL query. The route is the public order lookup page and needs no login. Sending `' OR '1'='1` returns every customer's orders. `UNION` payloads can also read other tables and the database schema. |
| F-002 | app/main.py:31 | Not exploitable | None | The user's input is only used to look up a value in a fixed list (`REPORT_STATUSES.get(key, "OPEN")`, main.py:8-12, 29). The query can only ever contain `OPEN`, `SHIPPED` or `REFUNDED`. |
| F-003 | tests/test_search.py:13 | Not exploitable | None | This is test setup code. Its values come from a hardcoded list and a loop counter, and it only runs against a temporary test database. No outside input reaches it. |

**What to do:**
- **F-001:** switch to a parameterized query (`WHERE customer_email = ?`). Also decide whether a public endpoint should hand out orders to anyone who knows an email address. That exposes customer data even after the injection is fixed.
- **F-002:** parameterizing it too would be a sensible precaution. Separately, I couldn't see any login check on this operations-dashboard endpoint, so someone should confirm whether it needs one.
- **F-003:** no fix needed. You could use placeholders anyway, or stop the scanner applying this rule to `tests/`.
